Honestly, I expected more from PAYDAY 2. The gameplay gets repetitive very quickly, the progression can feel frustrating, and some missions become more annoying than fun. citations.review_text:
[h1]PAYDAY 2 – 8/10. The Biggest Heist Was My DLC Budget.[/h1]
PAYDAY 2 gave me 82 hours of memorable heists, questionable decisions, excellent cooperative gameplay, and some genuinely great moments with my friends.

I loved the missions, the characters, and especially the surprisingly interesting lore behind the PAYDAY gang.
Unfortunately, I also watched a game I genuinely enjoyed become increasingly frustrating because of its endless stream of paid DLC.

[h2]One of the Best Cooperative Crime Experiences[/h2]
What made PAYDAY 2 special was the freedom to approach a robbery in different ways.

I loved preparing for stealth missions, bringing a suppressed pistol, carefully selecting my equipment, and trying to complete objectives without attracting unnecessary attention.

There was something satisfying about successfully bypassing security, coordinating with teammates, and escaping before anyone realised what had happened.

Of course, I also enjoyed bringing heavier weapons when things inevitably went wrong.
And when I played with my friend Filip, preparing for an absolute massacre was usually the more realistic strategy.

Our stealth plans occasionally had a shorter life expectancy than the security guards.
Sebastian, on the other hand, was much more interested in hacking and careful infiltration.

That contrast made playing together incredibly entertaining.

[h2]Diamond Heist, No Mercy, and the PAYDAY Universe[/h2]
Diamond Heist and No Mercy were among my absolute favourite missions.
I loved their atmosphere, objectives, and the way they contributed to the identity of the game.

PAYDAY 2 also had something I appreciated more than I initially expected: genuinely interesting lore.
The criminal underworld, recurring characters, mysterious connections, and gradually expanding story gave the robberies more personality than simply stealing money and escaping.

I particularly liked Clover, Sokol, John Wick, and, of course, Dallas.

The gang had character, and that made re…

Рекомендую ✅ 🕐 Наиграно: более 150 часов (я еще играл пирате так что можно еще это тоже в счёт)

Классический кооперативный шутер про ограбления, который держится на плаву уже больше десяти лет — и по-прежнему находит, чем удивить.

Что хорошо:

Геймплей. Стелс и штурм — два полноценных разных стиля игры. Тихий заход по маршруту и обходу камер, шумный — по позиционке и амуниции. Оба проработаны, и игра не заставляет играть только одним способом.
Прокачка. Древо скиллов, билды под стелс или штурм, огромный арсенал. Оптимизация билда сама по себе — половина удовольствия.
Контент. Десятки ограблений разных масштабов: от ограбления ювелирного до целых сюжетных кампаний. Карты узнаваемые, механики разнообразные.
Кооператив. Лучше всего раскрывается с друзьями. Случайные тиммейты — лотерея, но комьюнити живое, найти лобби не проблема.
Саундтрек. Динамичная музыка, которая нарастает вместе с давлением спецназа — сильная сторона игры.
Оптимизация. Игра тянет даже на слабом железе — спокойно идёт на видеокарте с 1–2 ГБ видеопамяти. Отличный вариант для не самых новых ПК.
Что не очень:

Донат и DLC. Единственный жирный минус: много контента фактически за деньги, а часть вещей честнее назвать микротранзакциями. Базовой игры хватает надолго, но докупать придётся.
Вердикт: 8/10. Отличный кооператив с большой глубиной и всё ещё живым сообществом. Идеален для компании из 2–4 человек, в одиночку тоже играбельно, но теряет часть магии. Тянет даже на слабых машинах, так что советую смело — если есть скидка, брать точно стоит.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as featuring a vast collection of heists with both stealth and loud approaches available.

citations.review_text: This game has very much options you can do stealth or loud you can make a plan to enter building it has DLC's I love this game and recommend to other players who loves Robbery and heist.

If you somehow haven't heard of Payday 2, do yourself two favors. Go watch Heat (1995) then go buy the edition of Payday 2 bundled with most of it's DLC on deep sale. Also pretend that Payday 3 doesn't exist, it's mediocre. Aside from GTA Online, I have never seen such elaborate heisting mechanics in a videogame to this damn day. 

The guns are plentiful and the attachment variety is unmatched, even by it's own sequel which falls into the trap of most guns feeling almost identical. You can play an entertaining cast of original characters, as well as John Wick, Ron Pearlman, some divorced lolcow, and many more. There are 50+ heists to master. Many of which with elaborate easter eggs to discover. You can go on a killing spree with a forklift. You can bring a loadout of nothing but weapons from the 1600's and it'll somehow still be effective.

The amount of dumb fun I've had with this game is almost too much to list. Don't let the dated graphics stop you from trying one of the greatest coop FPS games of all time. They don't make em like this anymore.

[h1] Payday 2 and the main reasons to buy/not buy the game [/h1]
[hr][/hr]
[h3] Disclaimer: this review may contain spoilers from the actual game in order to make it as accurate as possible [/h3]
[hr][/hr]
Payday 2 is a Multiplayer Co-op, PvE, FPS Heist game. The game present a lot of mechanics, different heists and weapons in which the Players can use. Despite presenting a lot of replayability, a vast majority of the game's assets are locked behind DLCs.
Because of these multiple replayability factors and the interaction between Players it can make them stick to the game for countless hours without losing it's fun factor. Payday 2 has a great number of guns and mods you can add to them as well as 7 core difficulties, different playstyles you can choose from, and over 70 playable heists. The heists contains a lot of different elements, tactics (Loud only, stealth only or stealth possible), objectives, and layouts that differentiate them from other missions as well as different enemies that appear on higher difficulties. The game can be pretty entertaining due to these diffent features.
However, most of the weapons and their mods, heists, characters, etc are locked behind DLCs. Despite being a good game, Payday 2 is heavily locked behind DLCs, making the experience for people that cannot afford it worse. The DLC problem makes the game feel like an "indirect Pay-To-Win" because in order to use some guns, perk decks, deployables, etc in which sometimes are needed for different builds are locked behind a paywall and Players who can't buy them may not be able to enjoy the full game. Due to this, it feels like the game is "excluding" Players for not buying the heavy amounts of DLCs.
In conclusion, the game can be pretty enjoyable and have a high amount of replayability but the DLCs can get on the way once you try to build a playstyle you are comfortable with. The game's DLC problem must be fixed, and not be more exploited by the Developers.

Four-player heists are the whole appeal, and it’s at its best with a crew that actually talks. You pick a job, plan your approach, and then either sneak in quietly or go loud with drills, hostages, and a very long fight waiting for the escape van. Nothing beats a stealth run going perfectly, except maybe the moment it all falls apart and everyone starts shooting. There’s a huge pile of skill trees, weapons, and masks to unlock, so there’s always something to work toward. The DLC and microtransactions can feel excessive, and it’s a lot more fun with friends than with random teammates, but for co-op chaos it holds up really well.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that a large amount of the game's weapons, mods, characters, and heists are locked behind DLC content.

citations.review_text: As of recently, it’s been a game I’ve been enjoying deeply (despite its controversy’s) game has its downs and lows but it’s just part of the experience, only complaint is the amount of content locked behind 3000000+ DLCS. But other than that I enjoy the mechanics. The collaborations are fun, despite SOME being a bit dated and aging like milk *cough cough* (H3H3 character pack). As somebody who is still somewhat new to payday2 on PC I just wanted to say that it’s an addicting experience when you can really get into it. Most of the gunplay feels great. I’m also happy sidetrack games has taken on payday 2 optimizing the game and adding even more content to the game! Amazing for a 13+ year old game. Also it’s nice to have an offline mode for the game.
